title: Security audit of secret-protection-core

workingTree.duringExecution: Unrelated uncommitted changes appeared across production sources, tests and documentation. They were preserved and excluded from baseline conclusions; later changed-source and replaced-artifact builds are not baseline results.

included: Every Rust source and test file
Secret memory, wiping, guard pages and closed pages
Apple and Windows platform code by static review
excluded: macOS, Windows, Android and iOS runtime execution

checks.result: 11 unit tests passed; isolation passed one check and then failed the shared-IPC assertion; later tests did not run

checks.command: cargo clippy --all-targets for host and all five rust-toolchain targets with -D warnings
checks.result: Host, WebAssembly, Windows, macOS, iOS and Android compiled; this is not runtime evidence

findings.title: Worker keeps inherited channels when both descriptor-closing methods fail
findings.evidence: A public-API harness refused close_range and supplied a synthetic /proc without self/fd. The worker retained an inherited socket and wrote byte [120] after isolation. Local inherited-fd log and command JSON.
findings.reproduction: Create an inheritable synthetic socket, refuse close_range with an earlier seccomp filter, hide /proc/self/fd while retaining /proc/self/exe, then start Worker and use that descriptor.
findings.expected: The worker has only its standard pipes or startup fails before a successful isolation report and any request.
findings.observed: close_inherited silently returned after both methods failed; the worker started and transmitted through the inherited socket.
findings.impact: A connected socket, writable file or other inherited descriptor remains a direct secret-egress channel in a restricted container or seccomp-confined program.
findings.recommendedFix: Make descriptor closure fallible and stop worker startup when neither close_range nor descriptor enumeration completes.
findings.requiredVerification: Repeat the live-socket probe and run ordinary close_range, /proc and /dev/fd fallback tests plus the worker suite on Linux and macOS.

findings.title: Sequential namespace calls leave IPC shared while network isolation succeeds
findings.evidence: Harness ipc returned exit 1 with empty_network true and IPC inode 4026531839 before and after. The stock isolation test failed the same assertion. Independent unshare commands confirmed sequential IPC failure and combined-flag success.
findings.reproduction: Compare /proc/self/ns/ipc before and after Isolation::enter on a single-threaded Linux process where user/network namespaces are available.
findings.expected: The documented IPC namespace is created or its absence is explicitly reported.
findings.observed: CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWNET succeeded, CLONE_NEWIPC failed with EPERM and its result was discarded; empty_network was true while IPC remained shared.
findings.impact: IPC objects remain shared. Seccomp mitigates this on x86-64/AArch64, but unsupported architectures lack that filter; the baseline mandatory test is red.
findings.recommendedFix: Request user, network and IPC namespaces atomically and avoid nested re-entry after success, or expose IPC failure separately.
findings.requiredVerification: Pass the stock whole-process test and positive/negative System V IPC and POSIX-queue probes on filtered and unfiltered architectures.

findings.title: Several advertised Windows protections discard their read-back results
findings.evidence: Source control flow discards mitigation results for extension points, image loading and child processes, ignores job setup and assignment, and discards lower_integrity's read-back. No Protection values represent them. Windows was not executed.
findings.reproduction: On a Windows context that refuses one of these operations, call Isolation::enter and inspect fields and measures. Static inspection shows no caller-visible state for the failure.
findings.expected: Every advertised protection is confirmed and reported, and required protections can fail strict mode.
findings.observed: The operations' failures cannot be distinguished from success through the public report even though documentation says they are applied.
findings.impact: Callers may rely on protections Windows refused. The audit does not assert which policy fails on a particular Windows build.
findings.recommendedFix: Expose confirmed state for every retained protection, include failures in strict mode and measures, and check job configuration and assignment.
findings.requiredVerification: Run success and forced-failure cases on supported Windows versions for child creation, UI restrictions, image loading and integrity.

findings.title: Dropping a worker after an oversized answer can deadlock both processes
findings.evidence: A 1 MiB synthetic answer with a 1 KiB caller limit produced InvalidData; Drop then exceeded a three-second watchdog. Local worker-drop log and command JSON.
findings.reproduction: Return a 1 MiB answer from serve, call Worker::call with most=1024, then drop the worker.
findings.expected: Error cleanup closes the worker and returns without draining an unbounded frame.
findings.observed: The parent stopped reading but kept its read pipe open; the child blocked on write while Drop closed only input and waited.
findings.impact: The response-size bound can cause permanent caller and worker blockage during ordinary error cleanup.
findings.recommendedFix: Close or shut down the parent read channel before waiting and ensure blocked children are terminated and reaped; mark partial-frame I/O failures broken.
findings.requiredVerification: Test responses above pipe capacity, partial frames and exit during writes on every worker platform without hangs or leftover processes.

findings.title: Overflowing protected-stack size panics instead of returning an error
findings.evidence: The stack-overflow harness caught an attempt-to-add-with-overflow panic. Local log and command JSON.
findings.expected: The io::Result API returns a size or allocation error.
findings.observed: next_multiple_of(page_size()) overflowed before WorkArea's checked allocation path.
findings.impact: A caller-triggered panic with bounded availability impact; no corruption or disclosure was found.
findings.recommendedFix: Use checked_next_multiple_of and map overflow to InvalidInput or OutOfMemory.
findings.requiredVerification: Test usize::MAX, page boundaries, zero and PTHREAD_STACK_MIN on supported Unix targets.

findings.title: Technical notes still describe shipped options as future work
findings.evidence: The limitations say sendmsg/file locks are future options and signals are blocked only from Linux 6.12; the test section says two programs although three exist.
findings.reproduction: Compare docs/TECHNICAL.md lines 167-184 with Options and Cargo.toml integration tests.
findings.expected: The document describes current options and actual test coverage.
findings.observed: Implemented options are described as future work and the test inventory/count is stale.
findings.impact: Readers can misunderstand available protections and test coverage; no direct runtime impact.
findings.recommendedFix: Update the limitation and test inventory, including signals, lock-all, channels, measures, protected stack and the new negative regressions.
findings.requiredVerification: Review final text against the final API and tests; no build is required for text alone.

limitations: Windows and macOS runtime behavior was not executed; Android and iOS were also not run.
The baseline full test command failed; no release acceptance is stated.
Initial stock-test and clippy console results are recorded in the report without timestamped local logs; retained reproduction commands have exact UTC records and hashes.
No assembly-level or exhaustive dependency-internal audit was performed; cargo-audit and cargo-deny were unavailable.
Unrelated working-tree changes that appeared during execution were not reviewed and were not used to invalidate or replace baseline evidence.
The audit does not claim absence of all vulnerabilities or independent cryptographic certification.
